senses.label: Climate of a region
senses.summary: A region's characteristic heat, cold and moisture, shaping the plants, animals and people that live there.
markers: a region's seasons, winds and waters shape what lives there

sources.note: How a region's seasons, winds and waters shape its people.

senses.label: Gases that hold in the earth's heat
senses.summary: The atmosphere retains the earth's heat, and certain gases, among them water vapour and carbonic acid, absorb radiant heat strongly.
markers: gases in the air hold in the earth's heat
hazards: The phrase 'greenhouse effect' is twentieth-century, but the concept is Fourier's (1824) and Tyndall's (from 1859); it is placed by concept, so a figure of 1824 or later saying it is not flagged.

sources.citation: Joseph Fourier, 'Remarques générales sur les températures du globe terrestre et des espaces planétaires' (1824)
sources.note: The atmosphere raises the earth's temperature by retaining heat.

sources.citation: John Tyndall, 'On the absorption and radiation of heat by gases and vapours', Philosophical Transactions (1861)
sources.note: Measured, from 1859, that water vapour and carbonic acid absorb radiant heat; speculated that changes in them produced past changes of climate.

senses.label: Human-caused warming
senses.summary: Burning fuel adds carbon dioxide to the air, and this is warming the whole planet.
markers: human burning of fuel is warming the whole planet
hazards: Bare 'climate change' and 'emissions' are deliberately not terms: changes of climate through geological time are an older idea (Darwin writes of them; Tyndall speculated on their cause), and 'emission' of heat and light is old physics. The modern sense is carried by the markers; an answer saying only 'climate change' is a known gap for term matching.

sources.citation: Svante Arrhenius, Världarnas utveckling (1906); English, Worlds in the Making (1908)
sources.note: Presented the idea that carbon dioxide from burning fossil fuels could raise the average global temperature.

sources.citation: G. S. Callendar, 'The artificial production of carbon dioxide and its influence on temperature', Quarterly Journal of the Royal Meteorological Society 64 (1938)
sources.note: First to link measured warming to fuel combustion.

senses.label: International climate policy
senses.summary: Nations act together on climate change: cutting emissions, adapting to its effects, and paying for losses that cannot be prevented.
markers: wealthy nations owe help to those harmed by a changing climate
hazards: Bare 'adaptation' is never a term: it is Darwin's own central word, in its biological sense. Only 'climate adaptation' signals this sense.

sources.citation: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (1992)
Vanuatu, for the Alliance of Small Island States, proposal to the Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee (December 1991)
sources.note: Proposed an international insurance pool for loss and damage; the origin of the concept.
